The Broncos, led by tenth-year head coach [[Herb Sendek]], played their home games at the [[Leavey Center]] as members of the [[West Coast Conference]]. On July 21, 2025, the Broncos and Sendek agreed to an extension that last until the end of the 2029–30 season.{{cite web|url=https://santaclarabroncos.com/news/2025/7/21/mens-basketball-herb-sendeks-contract-extended-through-2030.aspx|title=Herb Sendek's Contract Extended Through 2030|work=santaclarabroncos.com |date=July 21, 2025 }} ==Previous season== The [[2024–25 Santa Clara Broncos men's basketball team|Broncos]] finished the [[2024–25 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2024–25 season]] 21–13, 12–6 in WCC play to finish in fourth place.{{Cite web |title=2024-25 Santa Clara Broncos Men's Schedule and Results |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/schools/santa-clara/men/2025-schedule.html |access-date=2025-10-22 |website=College Basketball at Sports-Reference.com |language=en}} In the [[2024 West Coast Conference men's basketball tournament|WCC tournament]], they were upset in the first round by [[2024-25 Pepperdine Waves men's basketball team|Perpperdine]] in the quarterfinals.{{Cite web |title=Pepperdine vs. Santa Clara Box Score (Men), March 9, 2025 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/boxscores/2025-03-09-20-santa-clara.html |access-date=2025-10-22 |website=College Basketball at Sports-Reference.com |language=en}} They received an at-large bid to the [[2025 National Invitation Tournament|National Invitation Tournament]] as the No. 2 seed in the Irvine Region. They defeated [[2024–25 UC Riverside Highlanders men's basketball team|UC Riverside]] 101–62 to record their first NIT win in 41 years before falling to [[2024–25 UAB Blazers men's basketball team|UAB]] 88–84 in the second round. ==Offseason== ===Departures=== {| class="wikitable sortable" border="1" !
